title: Document management (DMS) and the EMC/OpenText case

videos.script: Every batch of milk Serra Alta sells leaves a trail of documents behind it. {{batch}} A lab result, a certificate of analysis, the procedure the operators followed that morning. When a supermarket asks for the certificate of one batch, somebody has to find it in minutes. And it has to be the right version. {{folder}} This lesson starts with why a shared folder cannot do that job. Versions, approval, search and a trail of who did what are what a document management system adds. {{retention}} Then records. Some documents are evidence, and evidence is kept for a set time and then destroyed on purpose. Keeping everything forever is not the safe choice it looks like. {{owners}} Serra Alta bought its system from EMC in 2010. Today it pays OpenText for it, and nobody at Serra Alta chose that. The product changed owners twice while the company was using it. {{links}} Last, the part an architect designs. A document belongs to something in the ERP, a batch or a supplier. How you link the two decides whether the certificate can still be found in five years. Like the other vendor lessons, this one is taught from documentation, and there is nothing to install.
